note_plain:
S:
  2 week Hx exertional central chest tightness/pressure
  Triggered by exertion (pushing wheelbarrow, climbing stairs)
  Lasts 5-10 mins, resolves with rest
  Radiated to left arm once
  No pain at rest
  Mild SOB with pain, no nausea/vomiting
  Occasional post-prandial burning (rice), different from current pain
  No chest wall tenderness on palpation
  Smokes 20 cigarettes/day for 30 years
  Alcohol: weekends, 2-3 glasses
  Hx of high BP diagnosed last year at medical camp, untreated
  Father had MI age ~60
  No regular medications or known allergies

O:
  Pulse 88/min, regular
  BP 150/95 mmHg
  Heart sounds normal, no murmurs
  Lungs clear
  No chest wall tenderness on palpation

A:
  Concerned for angina pectoris
  Hypertension (newly diagnosed)

P:
  ECG now
  Urgent referral to Cardiology clinic
  Start Aspirin (dose unspecified) after ECG
  Smoking cessation advice, provide details of clinics
  Address hypertension - monitor BP, likely start medication
  Safety-netting: If chest pain occurs at rest >15 mins & not settling, go straight to hospital ED

missed: Key negatives: no cough or cold symptoms
note_plain:
S:
  6yo F presents with 3 days fever (started Fri eve).
  Fever up to 39°C, responds partially to paracetamol.
  Associated headache and retro-orbital pain.
  Vomiting x2 this morning.
  Anorexia.
  Reduced fluid intake.
  Passing urine normally.
  No rash, bleeding (gums, nose, urine, stool).
  Mild cough.
  No ear pain.
  Local dengue outbreak reported.
  Construction site nearby with water collection.
  No previous history of dengue.
  Otherwise healthy child, no allergies.
  Currently taking paracetamol.

O:
  Temp 38.9°C.
  Mild conjunctival injection.
  Throat slightly red.
  Chest clear on auscultation.
  Abdomen soft, non-tender, liver not enlarged.
  No rash or petechiae.
  Capillary refill normal.
  Alert and appears well hydrated.

A:
  Fever, 3 days duration.
  Possible Dengue Fever (given symptoms & local epidemiology).
  Viral fever differential.

P:
  Full Blood Count (FBC).
  Dengue NS1 test.
  Paracetamol for fever ONLY. Avoid ibuprofen/NSAIDs.
  Encourage oral fluids frequently (water, king coconut, kanji).
  Review tomorrow with blood results.
  Safety netting: return immediately / go to hospital if worsening symptoms (severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, lethargy/confusion, oliguria, cold extremities) or sudden deterioration after fever subsides.

S:
  3 month diabetes check-up
  Feels generally 'not too bad'
  Reports increased thirst
  Burning, tingling feet at night for ~2 months, wakes her up
  Symptoms in both feet equally
  Some numbness in feet ('walking on cushions')
  No wounds or ulcers on feet; checks regularly
  Medications: Metformin 1g BD, Gliclazide 80mg AM, Losartan 50mg OD
  No episodes of hypoglycaemia (shaking, sweating, faintness)
  Checks blood sugar at home; fasting ~160-170 mg/dL
  Diet: Rice in afternoon, bread/string hoppers at night. Tea with 2 tsp sugar BD
  No regular exercise due to knee pain
  No chest pain or breathlessness
  Eyes 'alright' but no check >1 year

O:
  BP 140/85 mmHg
  Weight 68 kg
  Feet: Skin healthy, no cracks/ulcers. Pulses palpable bilaterally
  Neuropathy screen: Reduced sensation to monofilament in toes and ankle

A:
  Poorly controlled T2DM (HbA1c 8.4, fasting ~160-170)
  Diabetic peripheral neuropathy
  Hypertension (controlled on Losartan)

P:
  Increase Gliclazide to 80mg BD
  Start Atorvastatin 1mg nocte
  Order HbA1c, kidney function tests, cholesterol, urine protein
  Referral for diabetic eye screening
  Dietary advice: Reduce rice by half (replace with vegetables), eliminate sugar from tea
  Exercise advice: Start walking 15 mins daily on flat ground
  Foot care advice: Daily inspection for wounds/changes
  Review in 3 months with results

missed: Key negatives: speaking in full sentences
note_plain:
S:
  Asthma symptoms worsening over 1 month
  Wheezing, nocturnal cough (wakes ~2x/week)
  Using salbutamol 4-5x/week, sometimes twice daily
  Ran out of salbutamol last week
  No current preventer inhaler use (brown/orange)
  Triggers: dust (sweeping), dry weather, stress (exams)
  No recent fever, cold resolved 2 weeks ago
  No chest pain
  Can walk normally
  Hospital admission for asthma once as a child (overnight)
  Never ICU, no repeated nebulisers
  Non-smoker
  No household smokers

O:
  RR 18/min
  SpO2 98% on room air
  Mild expiratory wheeze bilaterally
  Peak flow 380 (expected ~450)

A:
  Uncontrolled asthma

P:
  Start beclometasone MDI 2 puffs AM + 2 puffs PM daily
  Provide spacer device
  Educate on correct inhaler technique with spacer
  Advise rinsing mouth after beclometasone use
  Environmental advice: wet-dusting, mask if sweeping
  Provide written asthma action plan
  Safety netting: seek immediate medical attention for severe breathlessness unresponsive to salbutamol
  Review in 1 month (peak flow, symptom control)

note_plain:
S:
  6 week hx burning epigastric pain
  Pain worse when hungry & at night (wakes patient)
  Pain relieved by food/Gelusil
  Pain radiates slightly up chest after late meals
  No weight loss, appetite normal
  No dysphagia
  No vomiting, haematemesis, or coffee ground vomitus
  Stools normal colour, no melena
  Takes ibuprofen 3-4 days/week (sometimes more) for back pain x >1 year
  Drinks arrack weekends (~quarter bottle/night)
  Non-smoker
  Irregular meals due to delivery work
  Reports job stress

O:
  Mild epigastric tenderness on palpation
  Abdomen otherwise soft, no lumps
  No pallor noted

A:
  Likely acid damage (irritation/ulcer) in stomach lining
  Exacerbated by ibuprofen use
  Contributing factors: empty stomach, alcohol, stress

P:
  Stop ibuprofen immediately
  Use paracetamol for back pain
  Start omeprazole 1 tab daily, 30 mins before breakfast x 4 weeks
  Stool test for H. pylori
  If H. pylori positive: add antibiotics (details not specified)
  Advice on regular meals (every 3-4 hrs)
  Advise reducing alcohol intake
  Follow up in 2 weeks with stool result
  Safety netting: attend hospital immediately if vomiting blood or melena
  Consider endoscopy if pain persists after 4 weeks or warning signs develop

S:
  Patient reports sudden onset R hand weakness yesterday evening (~6pm) lasting ~15 mins, associated with slurred speech. Symptoms resolved completely.
  No LOC, falls, fits or jerking movements during episode.
  No headache or visual disturbance reported.
  First such episode.
  Currently asymptomatic; denies weakness, facial droop, speech difficulty.
  History of HTN, takes amlodipine intermittently.
  Reports borderline T2DM and stopped cholesterol medication long ago.
  Smokes 5-6 cigarettes/day for 50 years.
  Reports occasional palpitations ('heart does a little dance').

O:
  BP 165/95 mmHg.
  Pulse irregularly irregular.
  Neurological exam: Strength equal in both hands. Facial symmetry intact. Speech clear ('British constitution'). No arm drift.
  Cardiac auscultation: Irregular rhythm, no murmurs.
  Lungs clear.

A:
  Transient Ischaemic Attack (TIA).
  Hypertension.
  Suspected Atrial Fibrillation.
  History of smoking.

P:
  ECG performed in clinic.
  Aspirin 300mg given immediately.
  Urgent referral to Medical Assessment Unit at Base Hospital today for brain scan and anticoagulation initiation.
  Safety netting: Advised patient to attend ED immediately if any neurological symptoms recur.

S:
  6 week hx burning epigastric pain, worse when hungry/at night, relieved by food/Gelusil.
  New onset melena x 2 days (black tarry stools, sticky).
  Associated postural dizziness, near-syncope this morning.
  Sweating, weakness.
  Mild SOB on exertion (stairs) today.
  Regular ibuprofen use for back pain >1 year, 3-4 days/week sometimes more.
  Weekend alcohol use (arrack, quarter bottle+).
  No known previous ulcer.
  No blood thinners/aspirin.
  No vomiting or haematemesis reported.
  No chest pain.

O:
  Pale conjunctivae.
  BP 100/70.
  Pulse 104 bpm.
  Epigastric tenderness on palpation.

A:
  Likely bleeding peptic ulcer (gastric).
  Significant blood loss / anaemia.
  NSAID-induced gastropathy.

P:
  Urgent hospital admission via ambulance.
  Referral letter to hospital.
  Investigations: Blood count, cross-match blood, urgent endoscopy.
  Management: IV fluids, possible transfusion.
  Stop ibuprofen immediately.
  Safety netting: Advise patient to inform ambulance crew if vomiting blood or feeling faint.

  No fever, chills, phlegm

  Chest clear to auscultation

S:
  6yo F presents with 4 days fever.
  Acute change today: drowsy, not waking properly.
  Refusing fluids (water, king coconut) since this morning.
  Vomited x4 since last night.
  Last urine output ~5am this morning.
  No bleeding (gums, nose, vomit).
  No rash observed by mother.
  Mother notes blotchy skin on legs, cold hands/feet, hot body.
  Cold extremities noted ~1 hour ago.
  No fits or shaking.
  Dengue contact in lane (neighbour recovered), 2 more houses now have fever.
  Mother notes child is drowsy, mumbles, asked strange question ('where school bag?').

O:
  Rousable but very drowsy.
  Temp 39.5C.
  Hands cold to wrists, body hot.
  Capillary refill time 4 seconds.
  Pulse 145/min, weak.
  Legs mottled.
  Abdomen: winces slightly on palpation.
  Neck: no stiffness.
  No rash or petechiae observed.

A:
  Shock (likely secondary to severe dengue or serious bacterial infection).

P:
  Immediate transfer to General Hospital via ambulance.
  Call ambulance (1990) - child in shock, suspected severe dengue.
  Referral note for hospital team: fever x4d, shock signs from morning, dengue contact.
  NPO (nothing by mouth).
  Positioning: flat, legs slightly elevated.
  Reassurance to mother.

note_plain:
S:
  15yo M presents with acute onset R lower abdominal pain radiating to R groin/testicle since 5 am this morning.
  Pain started suddenly, severe ('like a cricket ball hit me'), woke him from sleep.
  Initially came in waves, now constant.
  Associated nausea and vomiting x2 (home & en route).
  No fever, chills reported.
  Bowel movements normal yesterday, no diarrhoea/constipation.
  Urination normal, no dysuria or haematuria.
  No recent injury, fall, or trauma. Played cricket yesterday evening without incident.
  No unusual food intake. No other household members unwell.
  Pain radiates to R groin/testicle, possibly worse than abdominal pain. Pain exacerbated by underwear contact.

O:
  Patient in apparent distress due to pain.
  Abdomen: Tenderness on deep palpation R lower quadrant. No guarding/rebound noted (implied by 'soft' and lack of further comment).
  Genitalia: R testicle swollen, high-riding compared to L.
  R testicle exquisitely tender on palpation.
  Absent cremasteric reflex on R side. Present on L side.

A:
  Right testicular torsion.

P:
  Urgent surgical referral to hospital.
  Nil by mouth (NBM) immediately.
  Inform mother of situation and arrange hospital transport via uncle.
  Provide referral letter to surgical team.
  Patient safety-netting: Advise patient to report any future testicular pain immediately.
